result.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification
result.summary: Multi-agent systems for scientific claim verification increasingly rely on role-structured LLM debate to pressure-test hypotheses. However, when debating agents are instantiated from the same underlying base model, they share identical latent representations, making self-critique bias structurally inevitable. Static fixed-iteration protocols compound this by either halting prematurely before evidence stabilizes or wasting inference compute after convergence. We present \sys{}, a multi-agent research verification framework that addresses both failure modes. First, we introduce an asymmetric role architecture comprising an Advocate, Skeptic, and Arbitrator with opposing epistemic directives, producing significantly lower role-embedding similarity (0.852 vs.\ 0.918 for symmetric Multi-Agent Debate [MAD], $p = 5.82 \times 10^{-8}$) and surfacing more contested claims (22.0\% vs.\ 15.4\%). Second, we propose the Belief-Delta ($\DB$) convergence criterion, an evidence-grounded stopping rule that eliminates over-iteration (0.0\% vs.\ 62.5\% for Fixed-$3$) while cutting LLM calls by 2.4$\times$. Third, each supported claim is anchored to a verbatim literature snippet audited by an independent NLI classifier, achieving a 21.7\% hallucination rate (comparable to 25.9\% for a Self-Refine critic, $p = 0.61$) while establishing auditable evidence grounding. Across 200 runs on 40 research hypotheses evaluated with DeepSeek-R1-32B, \sys{} balances compute efficiency with rigorous epistemic verification.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一个多智能体科研主张验证框架：用 Advocate、Skeptic、Arbitrator 的非对称角色降低角色嵌入相似度，以 Belief-Delta 收敛准则替代固定迭代停止，并用独立 NLI 分类器审计逐字证据片段。
AI.relevance_reason: 其证据驱动的停止规则与证据锚定审计，可供核查 LVR 中 STOP 决策和视觉证据筛选的设计；角色嵌入相似度的度量方式也可能为 latent 相似度分析提供参照，但任务为纯文本验证，与视觉推理尚无直接联系。
